title: Adolescent with depressive symptoms: assess for suicidal ideation first
vignette: A 16-year-old boy is brought to the office for a well-child visit. The patient has no medical history but reports that his appetite is low and he has lost 2.3 kg (5 lb). He stopped playing soccer recently due to lack of interest. The patient is also worried about his grades due to difficulty staying focused in class and concentrating on his homework after school. He feels tired despite sleeping 10 hours a night and taking afternoon naps when he gets home. The patient says, "My parents try to be supportive, but everything they say these days gets on my nerves." He has tried alcohol and marijuana a few times at parties but does not use other drugs. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management of this patient?

clues.note: Loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (anhedonia) is a core feature of a major depressive episode.
Impaired concentration is one of the neurovegetative symptoms of depression (SIG E CAPS).

clues.text: everything they say these days gets on my nerves
clues.note: IRRITABILITY (rather than overt sadness) is a common presentation of depression in ADOLESCENTS.

whatMatters: Anhedonia, weight loss, poor concentration, hypersomnia/fatigue, and irritability = adolescent DEPRESSION. Because suicide is a leading cause of adolescent death and has immediate safety implications, the most appropriate next step is to ASSESS for SUICIDAL IDEATION. Answer E.
strategy: Recognize adolescent depression (irritable mood, anhedonia, neurovegetative symptoms) and prioritize SAFETY: directly ask about SUICIDAL THOUGHTS. Reject workups/steps that are lower priority or premature: ADHD rating scale (concentration issue is part of depression, ADHD is chronic/earlier onset), speaking with parents (assess the patient/safety first, confidentiality), CBC/thyroid (labs to exclude medical causes take time and are low-yield with a normal exam - safety is immediate), and urine drug screen (he's forthcoming; low yield, may harm rapport).

options.text: Administer an attention deficit hyperactivity disorder rating scale
Ask to speak with the patient's parents

eliminations.label: ADHD rating scale - concentration is part of depression
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: screening for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: his concentration difficulty is one of several depressive symptoms; ADHD has chronic symptoms with onset before adolescence, and safety takes priority. ✅ Correct if: chronic inattention/hyperactivity since childhood.

eliminations.label: Speak with parents - assess patient/safety first
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: involving the parents before assessing the patient. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's inappropriate to involve parents before fully assessing the adolescent (and his safety), and confidentiality should be respected. ✅ Correct if: after assessing the patient, with the patient's involvement/consent.

eliminations.label: Check CBC - low yield, takes time
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: laboratory workup for anemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: labs to exclude medical mimics take time and are low-yield with a normal history/exam; suicidality is the immediate concern. ✅ Correct if: signs pointing to anemia (fatigue with pallor).

eliminations.label: Check thyroid function - low yield, delayed
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: TSH to exclude thyroid disease. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: reasonable eventually to rule out medical causes, but results take time and safety comes first. ✅ Correct if: thyroid symptoms/signs suggesting hypo-/hyperthyroidism.

eliminations.label: Urine drug screen - forthcoming patient, harms rapport
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: testing for drugs of abuse. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: he is forthcoming about occasional use with no signs of intoxication; screening is unlikely to help and may damage the therapeutic relationship. ✅ Correct if: suspected concealed substance use with intoxication/impairment.

reasoning: Irritable mood, anhedonia, weight loss, poor concentration, and hypersomnia = adolescent depression
Suicide is a leading cause of death in adolescents and has immediate safety implications
Any adolescent with depressive/behavioral changes should be assessed for suicidal ideation
-> inquire about suicidal thoughts; answer E
mechanism: Adolescents with MAJOR DEPRESSION often present with IRRITABILITY (rather than overtly depressed mood), ANHEDONIA (loss of interest - e.g., quitting soccer), declining academic performance/concentration, changes in sleep and appetite/weight, fatigue, social withdrawal, and feelings of worthlessness/guilt (mnemonic SIG E CAPS). This 16-year-old meets that pattern. SUICIDE is among the LEADING CAUSES of death in adolescents (ages 15-19), and suicidal ideation has an IMMEDIATE impact on SAFETY and acute management (an actively suicidal patient may require hospitalization). Therefore the initial evaluation of any child/adolescent with suspected depression MUST include a careful SUICIDE-RISK ASSESSMENT - directly inquiring about suicidal thoughts, plans, and intent. Other steps (medical labs to exclude hypothyroidism/anemia, ADHD or substance evaluation, or involving parents) are lower priority than establishing immediate safety. (This is a sensitive topic; if this resonates personally, please know that support is available and I can help you find appropriate resources.)

difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > adolescent depression: irritability, anhedonia, declining grades, sleep/appetite change, withdrawal; assess suicide risk first (leading cause of adolescent death); labs (thyroid/anemia) low priority; respect confidentiality.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Adolescent depression -> safety first -> assess for suicidal ideation.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on adolescent depression, anhedonia, SIG E CAPS, or suicide risk assessment? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: ADHD/CBC/thyroid/drug screen are lower priority or premature; involving parents before assessing the patient is inappropriate.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: any adolescent with depressive symptoms -> screen for suicidal ideation first (immediate safety).
